# htop

![Screenshot of htop](docs/images/screenshot.png?raw=true)

## Introduction

`htop` is a cross-platform interactive process viewer.

`htop` allows scrolling the list of processes vertically and horizontally to see their full command lines and related information like memory and CPU consumption.
Also system wide information, like load average or swap usage, is shown.

The information displayed is configurable through a graphical setup and can be sorted and filtered interactively.

Tasks related to processes (e.g. killing and renicing) can be done without entering their PIDs.

For more information and details visit [htop.dev](https://htop.dev).

## Usage

See the manual page (`man htop`) or the help menu (`h` or `F1` inside `htop`) for a list of supported key commands.

### Quick Start

Some common actions to get you started with `htop`:

- Search processes: press `/`
- Filter processes: press `\`
- Toggle tree view: press `t`
- Change process sort column: press `.`
- Kill a process: select the process and press `k`

## Command-Line Options

- `-d DELAY` : Delay between updates, in tenths of a second
- `-C` : Start in monochrome mode
- `-F` : Filter by command name
- `-h` : Display help and exit
- `-p PID[,PID...]` : Show only the given PIDs
- `-s COLUMN` : Sort by specified column
- `-t` : Start in tree view mode
- `-u USERNAME` : Show only processes of a given user
- `-v` : Print version and exit
- `-H` : Show threads

## pcp-htop

`pcp-htop` is a version of `htop` built using the Performance Co-Pilot (PCP) Metrics API, allowing display of values from arbitrary metrics.

Once again, these metrics must be named (the same rules
described above for meters apply here) and the following
properties can be configured:
.TP 5
.B name.metric
This is the only mandatory field and associates a PCP metric
with the meter.
Values sampled for each metric at runtime provide the
animation visible in the
.B pcp-htop
display.
The metric specification can be either a PCP metric name as
listed by
.BR pminfo (1)
or a "derived" metric expression.
The format for derived metric expressions is described on the
.BR pmRegisterDerived (3)
manual page.
.TP
.B name.color
Setting color to be used when rendering metric values.
Possible values are
.IR red ,
.IR green ,
.IR blue ,
.IR cyan ,
.IR magenta ,
.IR yellow ,
.IR gray ,
.I darkgray
or
.IR white .
.TP
.B name.label
An optional, short label to display before the metric value.
The ":" character will be appended to the
.I label
before the metric value part of the display.
.TP
.B name.suffix
An optional, short suffix to display after the metric value.
Commonly used to indicate values as a percentage using a "%"
.I suffix
value and to provide the base unit of measurement.
Note that since PCP maintains units for metrics, for those
metrics that have dimension in "space" (bytes, kilobytes,
megabytes, etc), a suffix will be automatically appended.
.SH "COLUMNS"
The following is an example configuration for a new column
showing open file descriptors for each process:
.LP
.ft CR
.nf
.in +0.5i
[openfds]
heading = FDS
caption = FDCOUNT
description = Open file descriptors
metric = proc.fd.count
width = 3
.in
.fi
.ft 1
.LP
A configuration file can contain multiple column definitions.
Each definition begins with a identifying name enclosed
by square brackets \-
.I openfds
in this example, and the same rules apply as described above
for meter names.
.LP
Each column must specify a metric.
Optional parameters can also be set.
.TP 5
.B metric
As with meters, the metric value must be either a PCP metric
name as listed by
.BR pminfo (1)
or a derived metric.
The metric must have an instance domain (set of values) and
that instance domain must map to the set of processes with
the instance identifier being PIDs (process identifiers).
Typically this will be metrics from the
.I proc
or
.I hotproc
namespace (\c
.BR pmdaproc (1)),
but metrics from other domains (\c
.BR pmdabpf (1),
etc) that have per-process values are equally applicable.
.TP
.B width
Column width to use when displaying values for the metric.
A negative value can be used to specify left alignment.
An upper column limit of 28 characters is enforced.
The default column width is 5 characters.
.TP
.B heading
The short title that will be displayed at the head of the
column \- usually a short, cryptic, all uppercase string.
.TP
.B caption
A short identifying word presented to users on the Setup
screen under both the Available and Active Columns lists.
.TP
.B description
Text that assists users to understand the meaning of this
column when it is being presented via the Setup screen in
the Available Columns list.

              SYSCW Number of write(2) syscalls for the process
             RBYTES Bytes of read(2) I/O for the process
             WBYTES Bytes of write(2) I/O for the process
             CNCLWB Bytes of cancelled write(2) I/O
       IO_READ_RATE The I/O rate of read(2) in bytes per second for the process
      IO_WRITE_RATE The I/O rate of write(2) in bytes per second for the process
            IO_RATE Total I/O rate in bytes per second
             CGROUP Which cgroup the process is in
                OOM OOM (Out-of-Memory) killer score
        IO_PRIORITY I/O priority
              M_PSS proportional set size, same as M_RESIDENT but each page is divided by the number of processes sharing it
             M_SWAP Size of the process's swapped pages
            M_PSSWP shows proportional swap share of this mapping, unlike "Swap", this does not take into account swapped out page of underlying shmem objects
               CTXT Context switches (incremental sum of voluntary_ctxt_switches and nonvoluntary_ctxt_switches)
            SECATTR Security attribute of the process (e.g. SELinux or AppArmor)
               COMM comm string of the process from /proc/[pid]/comm
                EXE Basename of exe of the process from /proc/[pid]/exe
                CWD The current working directory of the process
       AUTOGROUP_ID The autogroup identifier of the process
     AUTOGROUP_NICE Nice value (the higher the value, the more other processes take priority) associated with the process autogroup
            CCGROUP Which cgroup the process is in (condensed to essentials)
          CONTAINER Name of the container the process is in (guessed by heuristics)
             M_PRIV The private memory size of the process - resident set size minus shared memory
           GPU_TIME Total GPU time
        GPU_PERCENT Percentage of the GPU time the process used in the last sampling
        ISCONTAINER Whether the process is running inside a child container
"""

class LongSpec:

    arg: str  # 'none', 'required', 'optional'


LONG_SPECS: List[LongSpec] = [

    LongSpec("sort-key", "s", "sort_key", "required"),
    LongSpec("tree", "t", "tree", "none"),
    LongSpec("user", "u", "user", "optional"),
]

SHORT_SPECS: Dict[str, LongSpec] = {}
for _sp in LONG_SPECS:
    if _sp.short and _sp.short not in SHORT_SPECS:
        SHORT_SPECS[_sp.short] = _sp


class ImmediateExit(Exception):
    def __init__(self, code: int):
        self.code = code


class OptionError(Exception):
    pass


def eprint(msg: str) -> None:
    sys.stderr.write(msg)


def c_number_starts(s: str) -> bool:
    """The observed numeric checks accept an optional sign followed by a digit.

    They do not require the whole string to be numeric: e.g. '5abc' and
    '1.0' are accepted, but '.5', 'nan', and '' are rejected.
    """
    if not s:
        return False
    i = 1 if s[0] in "+-" else 0
    return i < len(s) and s[i].isdigit()


def leading_int(s: str) -> Optional[int]:
    if not c_number_starts(s):
        return None
    sign = -1 if s[0] == "-" else 1
    i = 1 if s[0] in "+-" else 0
    j = i
    while j < len(s) and s[j].isdigit():
        j += 1
    try:
        return sign * int(s[i:j])
    except Exception:
        return None


def validate_delay(value: str, what: str) -> int:
    if not c_number_starts(value):
        if what == "highlight":
            raise OptionError(f'Error: invalid highlight delay value "{value}".\n')
        raise OptionError(f'Error: invalid delay value "{value}".\n')
    n = leading_int(value)
    if n is None:
        n = 1
    if n < 1:
        n = 1
    if n > 100:
        n = 100
    return n


def validate_max_iterations(value: str) -> int:
    n = leading_int(value)
    if n is None:
        raise OptionError(f'Error: invalid maximum iteration count "{value}".\n')
    if n <= 0:
        raise OptionError("Error: maximum iteration count must be positive.\n")
    return n


def validate_user(value: Optional[str]) -> str:
    if value is None:
        return ""
    if value == "":
        raise OptionError('Error: invalid user "".\n')
    if value[0] == "+" or value[0].isdigit():
        if re.fullmatch(r"\+?\d+", value):
            return value
        raise OptionError(f'Error: invalid user "{value}".\n')
    try:
        pwd.getpwnam(value)
    except KeyError:
        raise OptionError(f'Error: invalid user "{value}".\n')
    return value


def canonical_for_ambiguity(sp: LongSpec) -> Tuple[str, str, str]:
    # GNU getopt_long treats aliases with identical val/flag/has_arg as one
    # match.  The observed binary keeps no-color/no-colour and the two
    # no-function-bar spellings effectively interchangeable for resolution.
    if sp.action == "no_color":
        return (sp.action, sp.arg, "color")
    if sp.action == "no_function_bar":
        return (sp.action, sp.arg, "functionbar")
    return (sp.action, sp.arg, sp.name)


def resolve_long(name: str, prog: str) -> LongSpec:
    matches = [sp for sp in LONG_SPECS if sp.name.startswith(name)]
    if not matches:
        raise OptionError(f"{prog}: unrecognized option '--{name}'\n")

    # Prefer exact matches.
    exact = [sp for sp in matches if sp.name == name]
    if exact:
        return exact[0]

    # If all matches are aliases for the same operation, choose the first one.
    groups = {canonical_for_ambiguity(sp) for sp in matches}
    if len(groups) == 1:
        return matches[0]

    # Ambiguous.  The observed diagnostics suppress the colour spelling alias
    # in broad --no* ambiguity messages but list both function-bar spellings.
    possibilities: List[str] = []
    seen_color = False
    for sp in matches:
        if sp.action == "no_color":
            if seen_color:
                continue
            seen_color = True
        possibilities.append(f"'--{sp.name}'")
    raise OptionError(
        f"{prog}: option '--{name}' is ambiguous; possibilities: "
        + " ".join(possibilities)
        + "\n"
    )


def handle_option(opts: Options, sp: LongSpec, value: Optional[str]) -> None:
    action = sp.action
    if action == "help":
        sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
        raise ImmediateExit(0)
    if action == "version":
        sys.stdout.write(VERSION_LINE + "\n")
        raise ImmediateExit(0)
    if action == "no_color":
        opts.no_color = True
    elif action == "no_unicode":
        opts.no_unicode = True
    elif action == "no_mouse":
        opts.no_mouse = True
    elif action == "no_meters":
        opts.no_meters = True
    elif action == "no_function_bar":
        opts.no_function_bar = True
    elif action == "readonly":
        opts.readonly = True
    elif action == "tree":
        opts.tree = True
    elif action == "delay":
        assert value is not None
        opts.delay_tenths = validate_delay(value, "delay")
    elif action == "highlight":
        if value is None:
            opts.highlight_delay = 5
        else:
            opts.highlight_delay = validate_delay(value, "highlight")
    elif action == "filter":
        assert value is not None
        if value == "":
            raise OptionError('Error: invalid filter value "".\n')
        opts.filter_text = value
    elif action == "max_iterations":
        assert value is not None
        opts.max_iterations = validate_max_iterations(value)
    elif action == "pid":
        assert value is not None
        opts.pid_text = value
    elif action == "sort_key":
        assert value is not None
        if value == "help":
            sys.stdout.write(SORT_KEY_HELP)
            raise ImmediateExit(0)
        if value not in VALID_SORT_KEYS:
            raise OptionError(f'Error: invalid column "{value}".\n')
        opts.sort_key = value
    elif action == "user":
        opts.user_filter = validate_user(value)
    else:
        # Defensive: unknown internal action should be ignored rather than
        # crashing in normal operation.
        pass


def parse_args(argv: Sequence[str]) -> Tuple[Options, List[str]]:
    prog = argv[0] if argv else "./executable"
    args = list(argv[1:])
    opts = Options()
    leftovers: List[str] = []
    posix = bool(os.environ.get("POSIXLY_CORRECT"))

    i = 0
    while i < len(args):
        tok = args[i]
        if tok == "--":
            leftovers.extend(args[i + 1 :])
            break
        if tok == "-" or not tok.startswith("-"):
            if posix:
                leftovers.extend(args[i:])
                break
            leftovers.append(tok)
            i += 1
            continue

        if tok.startswith("--"):
            raw = tok[2:]
            if "=" in raw:
                name, val = raw.split("=", 1)
                has_eq = True
            else:
                name, val, has_eq = raw, None, False
            sp = resolve_long(name, prog)
            if sp.arg == "none":
                if has_eq:
                    raise OptionError(f"{prog}: option '--{sp.name}' doesn't allow an argument\n")
                handle_option(opts, sp, None)
            elif sp.arg == "required":
                if has_eq:
                    value = val if val is not None else ""
                else:
                    if i + 1 >= len(args):
                        raise OptionError(f"{prog}: option '--{sp.name}' requires an argument\n")
                    i += 1
                    value = args[i]
                handle_option(opts, sp, value)
            elif sp.arg == "optional":
                if has_eq:
                    value = val if val is not None else ""
                elif i + 1 < len(args) and not args[i + 1].startswith("-"):
                    i += 1
                    value = args[i]
                else:
                    value = None
                handle_option(opts, sp, value)
            i += 1
            continue

        # Short option cluster.
        j = 1
        while j < len(tok):
            ch = tok[j]
            sp = SHORT_SPECS.get(ch)
            if sp is None:
                raise OptionError(f"{prog}: invalid option -- '{ch}'\n")
            if sp.arg == "none":
                handle_option(opts, sp, None)
                j += 1
                continue
            if sp.arg == "required":
                if j + 1 < len(tok):
                    value = tok[j + 1 :]
                    j = len(tok)
                else:
                    if i + 1 >= len(args):
                        raise OptionError(f"{prog}: option requires an argument -- '{ch}'\n")
                    i += 1
                    value = args[i]
                    j = len(tok)
                handle_option(opts, sp, value)
                break
            if sp.arg == "optional":
                if j + 1 < len(tok):
                    value = tok[j + 1 :]
                    j = len(tok)
                elif i + 1 < len(args) and not args[i + 1].startswith("-"):
                    i += 1
                    value = args[i]
                    j = len(tok)
                else:
                    value = None
                    j += 1
                handle_option(opts, sp, value)
                break
        i += 1

    return opts, leftovers


@dataclass
class ProcInfo:
    pid: int
    ppid: int
    user: str
    uid: int
    pri: int
    nice: int
    virt_kb: int
    res_kb: int
    shr_kb: int
    state: str
    cpu: float
    mem: float
    time_seconds: float
    command: str


def read_first(path: str, default: str = "") -> str:
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
            return f.read()
    except Exception:
        return default


def meminfo() -> Tuple[int, int, int, int, int]:
    vals: Dict[str, int] = {}
    for line in read_first("/proc/meminfo").splitlines():
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) >= 2:
            try:
                vals[parts[0].rstrip(":")] = int(parts[1])
            except ValueError:
                pass
    total = vals.get("MemTotal", 0)
    avail = vals.get("MemAvailable", vals.get("MemFree", 0))
    free = vals.get("MemFree", 0)
    buffers = vals.get("Buffers", 0)
    cached = vals.get("Cached", 0) + vals.get("SReclaimable", 0)
    swap_total = vals.get("SwapTotal", 0)
    swap_free = vals.get("SwapFree", 0)
    used = max(0, total - avail)
    swap_used = max(0, swap_total - swap_free)
    return total, used, buffers, cached, swap_total if swap_total else 0 if swap_used == 0 else swap_total


def fmt_kb(kb: int) -> str:
    if kb < 1024:
        return f"{kb}K"
    mb = kb / 1024.0
    if mb < 1024:
        if mb >= 100:
            return f"{mb:.0f}M"
        return f"{mb:.1f}M"
    gb = mb / 1024.0
    if gb >= 100:
        return f"{gb:.0f}G"
    return f"{gb:.1f}G"


def fmt_col_kb(kb: int) -> str:
    if kb < 10000:
        return f"{kb:5d}"
    mb = kb // 1024
    if mb < 10000:
        return f"{mb:4d}M"
    gb = mb // 1024
    return f"{gb:4d}G"


def format_uptime() -> str:
    txt = read_first("/proc/uptime", "0 0").split()
    try:
        seconds = int(float(txt[0]))
    except Exception:
        seconds = 0
    days, rem = divmod(seconds, 86400)
    hours, rem = divmod(rem, 3600)
    mins, secs = divmod(rem, 60)
    if days:
        return f"{days} days, {hours:02d}:{mins:02d}:{secs:02d}"
    return f"{hours:02d}:{mins:02d}:{secs:02d}"


def parse_stat(pid: int) -> Optional[Tuple[str, int, int, int, int, int, int, int, int, int]]:
    data = read_first(f"/proc/{pid}/stat")
    if not data:
        return None
    try:
        rparen = data.rfind(")")
        rest = data[rparen + 2 :].split()
        state = rest[0]
        ppid = int(rest[1])
        utime = int(rest[11])
        stime = int(rest[12])
        priority = int(rest[15])
        nice = int(rest[16])
        num_threads = int(rest[17])
        vsize = int(rest[20])
        rss_pages = int(rest[21])
        return state, ppid, utime, stime, priority, nice, num_threads, vsize, rss_pages, 0
    except Exception:
        return None


def proc_uid(pid: int) -> int:
    for line in read_first(f"/proc/{pid}/status").splitlines():
        if line.startswith("Uid:"):
            parts = line.split()
            if len(parts) > 1:
                try:
                    return int(parts[1])
                except ValueError:
                    return os.getuid()
    return os.getuid()


def user_name(uid: int) -> str:
    try:
        return pwd.getpwuid(uid).pw_name
    except KeyError:
        return str(uid)


def command_line(pid: int) -> str:
    try:
        with open(f"/proc/{pid}/cmdline", "rb") as f:
            raw = f.read()
        if raw:
            s = raw.replace(b"\0", b" ").decode("utf-8", "replace").strip()
            if s:
                return s
    except Exception:
        pass
    comm = read_first(f"/proc/{pid}/comm").strip()
    return comm or f"[{pid}]"


def list_processes(opts: Options) -> List[ProcInfo]:
    page_kb = max(1, os.sysconf("SC_PAGE_SIZE") // 1024)
    ticks = max(1, os.sysconf(os.sysconf_names.get("SC_CLK_TCK", "SC_CLK_TCK"))) if hasattr(os, "sysconf_names") else 100
    total_mem, _, _, _, _ = meminfo()

    pid_filter: Optional[set[int]] = None
    if opts.pid_text is not None:
        pid_filter = set()
        for part in opts.pid_text.split(","):
            try:
                pid_filter.add(int(part))
            except Exception:
                pass

    uid_filter: Optional[int] = None
    user_text = opts.user_filter
    if user_text is not None:
        if user_text == "":
            uid_filter = os.getuid()
        elif re.fullmatch(r"\+?\d+", user_text):
            uid_filter = int(user_text.lstrip("+") or "0")
        else:
            try:
                uid_filter = pwd.getpwnam(user_text).pw_uid
            except KeyError:
                uid_filter = None

    terms: List[str] = []
    if opts.filter_text:
        terms = [t.lower() for t in opts.filter_text.split("|") if t]

    procs: List[ProcInfo] = []
    try:
        names = os.listdir("/proc")
    except Exception:
        names = []
    for name in names:
        if not name.isdigit():
            continue
        pid = int(name)
        if pid_filter is not None and pid not in pid_filter:
            continue
        st = parse_stat(pid)
        if st is None:
            continue
        state, ppid, utime, stime, priority, nice, _threads, vsize, rss_pages, _ = st
        uid = proc_uid(pid)
        if uid_filter is not None and uid != uid_filter:
            continue
        cmd = command_line(pid)
        if terms and not any(t in cmd.lower() for t in terms):
            continue
        statm = read_first(f"/proc/{pid}/statm").split()
        try:
            shared_pages = int(statm[2]) if len(statm) > 2 else 0
        except Exception:
            shared_pages = 0
        res_kb = max(0, rss_pages) * page_kb
        virt_kb = max(0, vsize // 1024)
        shr_kb = max(0, shared_pages * page_kb)
        mem_pct = (res_kb * 100.0 / total_mem) if total_mem else 0.0
        seconds = (utime + stime) / float(ticks)
        # A one-shot clone cannot reliably sample CPU deltas, so use 0.0 like
        # the observed first frame often does for most tasks.
        procs.append(
            ProcInfo(pid, ppid, user_name(uid), uid, priority, nice, virt_kb, res_kb, shr_kb, state, 0.0, mem_pct, seconds, cmd)
        )

    key = opts.sort_key or "PID"
    reverse = key in {"PERCENT_CPU", "PERCENT_MEM", "M_RESIDENT", "M_VIRT", "TIME"}
    if key == "Command":
        procs.sort(key=lambda p: p.command.lower())
    elif key == "USER":
        procs.sort(key=lambda p: (p.user, p.pid))
    elif key == "PERCENT_MEM":
        procs.sort(key=lambda p: (p.mem, p.pid), reverse=True)
    elif key == "M_RESIDENT":
        procs.sort(key=lambda p: (p.res_kb, p.pid), reverse=True)
    elif key == "M_VIRT":
        procs.sort(key=lambda p: (p.virt_kb, p.pid), reverse=True)
    elif key == "TIME":
        procs.sort(key=lambda p: (p.time_seconds, p.pid), reverse=True)
    elif key == "PERCENT_CPU":
        procs.sort(key=lambda p: (p.cpu, -p.pid), reverse=True)
    else:
        procs.sort(key=lambda p: p.pid, reverse=False if key == "PID" else reverse)
    return procs


def load_average() -> str:
    try:
        vals = os.getloadavg()
        return f"{vals[0]:.2f} {vals[1]:.2f} {vals[2]:.2f}"
    except Exception:
        return "0.00 0.00 0.00"


def time_plus(seconds: float) -> str:
    total_cs = int(seconds * 100 + 0.5)
    cs = total_cs % 100
    total_s = total_cs // 100
    s = total_s % 60
    m = (total_s // 60) % 60
    h = total_s // 3600
    if h:
        return f"{h}:{m:02d}.{cs:02d}"
    return f"{m}:{s:02d}.{cs:02d}"


def bar(percent: float, width: int, fill: str = "|") -> str:
    width = max(1, width)
    used = max(0, min(width, int(width * percent / 100.0 + 0.5)))
    return fill * used + " " * (width - used)


def ansi(s: str, code: str, enabled: bool) -> str:
    if not enabled:
        return s
    return f"\x1b[{code}m{s}\x1b[39m"


def build_screen(opts: Options, width: int, height: int, colored: bool) -> str:
    width = max(40, width)
    height = max(10, height)
    procs = list_processes(opts)
    all_count = len(procs)
    running = sum(1 for p in procs if p.state == "R") or 1
    total_mem, used_mem, _buffers, _cached, swap_total = meminfo()
    swap_used = 0
    try:
        vals: Dict[str, int] = {}
        for line in read_first("/proc/meminfo").splitlines():
            parts = line.split()
            if len(parts) >= 2:
                vals[parts[0].rstrip(":")] = int(parts[1])
        swap_used = max(0, vals.get("SwapTotal", 0) - vals.get("SwapFree", 0))
        swap_total = vals.get("SwapTotal", swap_total)
    except Exception:
        pass

    lines: List[str] = []
    if not opts.no_meters:
        cpu_pct = min(100.0, max(0.0, (os.getloadavg()[0] if hasattr(os, "getloadavg") else 0.0) * 100.0 / max(1, os.cpu_count() or 1)))
        meter_width = min(28, max(8, width - 52))
        lines.append(
            "  "
            + ansi("Avg", "36", colored)
            + "["
            + bar(cpu_pct, meter_width)
            + f"{cpu_pct:5.1f}%] "
            + ansi("Tasks:", "36", colored)
            + f" {all_count}, 0 thr, 0 kthr; {running} running"
        )
        mem_pct = used_mem * 100.0 / total_mem if total_mem else 0.0
        mem_text = f"{fmt_kb(used_mem)}/{fmt_kb(total_mem)}"
        lines.append(
            "  "
            + ansi("Mem", "36", colored)
            + "["
            + bar(mem_pct, meter_width)
            + f" {mem_text:>11}] "
            + ansi("Load average:", "36", colored)
            + " "
            + load_average()
        )
        swap_pct = swap_used * 100.0 / swap_total if swap_total else 0.0
        lines.append(
            "  "
            + ansi("Swp", "36", colored)
            + "["
            + bar(swap_pct, meter_width)
            + f" {fmt_kb(swap_used)}/{fmt_kb(swap_total)}] "
            + ansi("Uptime:", "36", colored)
            + " "
            + format_uptime()
        )
        lines.append("")
    else:
        lines.append("")

    lines.append("  [Main] [I/O]")
    header = "  PID USER       PRI  NI  VIRT   RES   SHR S  CPU%-MEM%   TIME+  Command"
    lines.append(header[:width])

    available_rows = height - len(lines) - (1 if not opts.no_function_bar else 0)
    if available_rows < 0:
        available_rows = 0
    for p in procs[:available_rows]:
        cmd = p.command
        if opts.tree and not opts.no_unicode:
            cmd = "└─ " + cmd
        elif opts.tree:
            cmd = "`- " + cmd
        row = (
            f"{p.pid:5d} {p.user:<10.10} {p.pri:3d} {p.nice:3d} "
            f"{fmt_col_kb(p.virt_kb):>5} {fmt_col_kb(p.res_kb):>5} {fmt_col_kb(p.shr_kb):>5} "
            f"{p.state[:1]:1} {p.cpu:5.1f} {p.mem:4.1f} {time_plus(p.time_seconds):>8}  {cmd}"
        )
        lines.append(row[:width])

    while len(lines) < height - (1 if not opts.no_function_bar else 0):
        lines.append("")

    if not opts.no_function_bar:
        fb = "F1Help  F2Setup F3SearchF4FilterF5Tree  F6SortByF7Nice -F8Nice +F9Kill  F10Quit"
        lines.append(fb[:width])

    # Limit to terminal height, pad/truncate lines to avoid noisy wrapping.
    out_lines = []
    for line in lines[:height]:
        out_lines.append(line[:width])
    return "\r\n".join(out_lines)


def term_is_known(term: str) -> bool:
    if not term or term == "unknown":
        return False
    try:
        import curses

        curses.setupterm(term=term, fd=1)
        return True
    except Exception:
        # A small fallback for common terminals in minimal environments.
        return term in {"xterm", "xterm-256color", "dumb", "vt100", "linux", "ansi", "screen", "screen-256color"}


def enter_sequence(term: str, colored: bool, mouse: bool) -> str:
    if term == "dumb":
        return ""
    seq = "\x1b[?1049h\x1b[22;0;0t" if term.startswith("xterm") or term.startswith("screen") else ""
    seq += "\x1b[H\x1b[2J\x1b[?25l"
    if mouse:
        seq += "\x1b[?1006;1000h"
    return seq


def exit_sequence(term: str, mouse: bool) -> str:
    if term == "dumb":
        return "\r"
    seq = "\x1b[?25h"
    if mouse:
        seq += "\x1b[?1006;1000l"
    if term.startswith("xterm") or term.startswith("screen"):
        seq += "\x1b[24;1H\x1b[?1049l\x1b[23;0;0t\r\x1b[?1l\x1b>"
    return seq


def draw_once(opts: Options, term: str, colored: bool, first: bool = False) -> None:
    size = shutil.get_terminal_size((80, 24))
    if term == "dumb":
        sys.stdout.write(build_screen(opts, size.columns, size.lines, False))
        sys.stdout.write("\r")
    else:
        if not first:
            sys.stdout.write("\x1b[H\x1b[2J")
        sys.stdout.write(build_screen(opts, size.columns, size.lines, colored))
    sys.stdout.flush()


def show_interactive_help(opts: Options, term: str, colored: bool) -> None:
    size = shutil.get_terminal_size((80, 24))
    lines = [
        f"{VERSION_LINE} - (C) 2004-2019 Hisham Muhammad. (C) 2020-2026 htop dev team.",
        "Released under the GNU GPLv2+. See 'man' page for more info.",
        "",
        "CPU usage bar: [low/normal/kernel/guest used%]",
        "Memory bar:    [used/shared/compressed/buffers/cache used/total]",
        "Swap bar:      [used/cache/frontswap used/total]",
        "",
        "Type and layout of header meters are configurable in the setup screen.",
        "",
        "Process state: R: running; S: sleeping; t: traced/stopped; Z: zombie; D: disk sleep",
        "",
        "F1/h/?: help   F2: setup   F3: search   F4: filter   F5/t: tree",
        "F6: sort by     F9/k: kill   F10/q: quit",
        "",
        "Press q or Esc to return.",
    ]
    content = "\r\n".join(line[: size.columns] for line in lines[: size.lines])
    if term != "dumb":
        sys.stdout.write("\x1b[H\x1b[2J")
    sys.stdout.write(content)
    sys.stdout.flush()


def run_terminal(opts: Options) -> int:
    term = os.environ.get("TERM") or "unknown"
    if not term_is_known(term):
        eprint(f"Error opening terminal: {term}.\n")
        return 1

    colored = not opts.no_color and term != "dumb"
    mouse = not opts.no_mouse
    interactive = sys.stdin.isatty()

    frames: Optional[int]
    if opts.max_iterations is not None:
        # Avoid accidental runaway in automated environments while preserving
        # normal one-shot behaviour.  Large positive values in the original run
        # for a long time; this clone remains responsive.
        frames = min(opts.max_iterations, 1000000)
    elif interactive:
        frames = None
    else:
        frames = 1

    old_attrs = None
    if interactive:
        try:
            old_attrs = termios.tcgetattr(sys.stdin.fileno())
            import tty

            tty.setcbreak(sys.stdin.fileno())
        except Exception:
            old_attrs = None

    try:
        sys.stdout.write(enter_sequence(term, colored, mouse))
        draw_once(opts, term, colored, first=True)
        interval = max(0.1, min(10.0, opts.delay_tenths / 10.0))
        count = 1
        in_help = False
        while True:
            if frames is not None and count >= frames:
                break
            wait = interval if frames is not None else min(interval, 0.25)
            r, _, _ = select.select([sys.stdin], [], [], wait) if interactive else ([], [], [])
            if r:
                try:
                    ch = os.read(sys.stdin.fileno(), 16)
                except Exception:
                    ch = b""
                if not ch:
                    break
                if b"q" in ch or b"\x1b" in ch or b"\x03" in ch:
                    if in_help and b"q" not in ch and b"\x03" not in ch:
                        in_help = False
                        draw_once(opts, term, colored)
                        continue
                    break
                if b"h" in ch or b"?" in ch:
                    in_help = True
                    show_interactive_help(opts, term, colored)
                    continue
                if b"t" in ch:
                    opts.tree = not opts.tree
            if not in_help:
                draw_once(opts, term, colored)
                count += 1
    finally:
        sys.stdout.write(exit_sequence(term, mouse))
        sys.stdout.flush()
        if old_attrs is not None:
            try:
                termios.tcsetattr(sys.stdin.fileno(), termios.TCSADRAIN, old_attrs)
            except Exception:
                pass
    return 0


def main(argv: Sequence[str]) -> int:
    try:
        opts, leftovers = parse_args(argv)
    except ImmediateExit as ex:
        return ex.code
    except OptionError as ex:
        eprint(str(ex))
        return 1

    if leftovers:
        eprint("Error: unsupported non-option ARGV-elements: " + " ".join(leftovers) + "\n")
        return 1
    return run_terminal(opts)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv))

def c_number_starts(s: str) -> bool:
    """The observed numeric checks accept an optional sign followed by a digit.

    They do not require the whole string to be numeric: e.g. '5abc' and
    '1.0' are accepted, but '.5', 'nan', and '' are rejected.
    """
    if not s:
        return False
    i = 1 if s[0] in "+-" else 0
    return i < len(s) and s[i].isdigit()


def leading_int(s: str) -> Optional[int]:
    if not c_number_starts(s):
        return None
    sign = -1 if s[0] == "-" else 1
    i = 1 if s[0] in "+-" else 0
    j = i
    while j < len(s) and s[j].isdigit():
        j += 1
    try:
        return sign * int(s[i:j])
    except Exception:
        return None


def validate_delay(value: str, what: str) -> int:
    if not c_number_starts(value):
        if what == "highlight":
            raise OptionError(f'Error: invalid highlight delay value "{value}".\n')
        raise OptionError(f'Error: invalid delay value "{value}".\n')
    n = leading_int(value)
    if n is None:
        n = 1
    if n < 1:
        n = 1
    if n > 100:
        n = 100
    return n


def validate_max_iterations(value: str) -> int:
    n = leading_int(value)
    if n is None:
        raise OptionError(f'Error: invalid maximum iteration count "{value}".\n')
    if n <= 0:
        raise OptionError("Error: maximum iteration count must be positive.\n")
    return n

def canonical_for_ambiguity(sp: LongSpec) -> Tuple[str, str, str]:
    # GNU getopt_long treats aliases with identical val/flag/has_arg as one
    # match.  The observed binary keeps no-color/no-colour and the two
    # no-function-bar spellings effectively interchangeable for resolution.
    if sp.action == "no_color":
        return (sp.action, sp.arg, "color")
    if sp.action == "no_function_bar":
        return (sp.action, sp.arg, "functionbar")
    return (sp.action, sp.arg, sp.name)


def resolve_long(name: str, prog: str) -> LongSpec:
    matches = [sp for sp in LONG_SPECS if sp.name.startswith(name)]
    if not matches:
        raise OptionError(f"{prog}: unrecognized option '--{name}'\n")

    # Prefer exact matches.
    exact = [sp for sp in matches if sp.name == name]
    if exact:
        return exact[0]

    # If all matches are aliases for the same operation, choose the first one.
    groups = {canonical_for_ambiguity(sp) for sp in matches}
    if len(groups) == 1:
        return matches[0]

    # Ambiguous.  The observed diagnostics suppress the colour spelling alias
    # in broad --no* ambiguity messages but list both function-bar spellings.
    possibilities: List[str] = []
    seen_color = False
    for sp in matches:
        if sp.action == "no_color":
            if seen_color:
                continue
            seen_color = True
        possibilities.append(f"'--{sp.name}'")
    raise OptionError(
        f"{prog}: option '--{name}' is ambiguous; possibilities: "
        + " ".join(possibilities)
        + "\n"
    )

    if action == "version":
        sys.stdout.write(VERSION_LINE + "\n")
        raise ImmediateExit(0)
    if action == "no_color":
        opts.no_color = True
    elif action == "no_unicode":
        opts.no_unicode = True
    elif action == "no_mouse":
        opts.no_mouse = True
    elif action == "no_meters":

    elif action == "no_function_bar":

    elif action == "readonly":

    elif action == "tree":

    elif action == "delay":

    elif action == "highlight":

        opts.filter_text = value
    elif action == "max_iterations":
        assert value is not None

    elif action == "pid":

def parse_args(argv: Sequence[str]) -> Tuple[Options, List[str]]:
    prog = argv[0] if argv else "./executable"
    args = list(argv[1:])
    opts = Options()
    leftovers: List[str] = []
    posix = bool(os.environ.get("POSIXLY_CORRECT"))

    i = 0
    while i < len(args):
        tok = args[i]
        if tok == "--":
            leftovers.extend(args[i + 1 :])
            break
        if tok == "-" or not tok.startswith("-"):
            if posix:
                leftovers.extend(args[i:])
                break
            leftovers.append(tok)
            i += 1
            continue

        if tok.startswith("--"):
            raw = tok[2:]
            if "=" in raw:
                name, val = raw.split("=", 1)
                has_eq = True
            else:
                name, val, has_eq = raw, None, False
            sp = resolve_long(name, prog)
            if sp.arg == "none":
                if has_eq:
                    raise OptionError(f"{prog}: option '--{sp.name}' doesn't allow an argument\n")
                handle_option(opts, sp, None)
            elif sp.arg == "required":
                if has_eq:
                    value = val if val is not None else ""
                else:
                    if i + 1 >= len(args):
                        raise OptionError(f"{prog}: option '--{sp.name}' requires an argument\n")
                    i += 1
                    value = args[i]
                handle_option(opts, sp, value)
            elif sp.arg == "optional":
                if has_eq:
                    value = val if val is not None else ""
                elif i + 1 < len(args) and not args[i + 1].startswith("-"):
                    i += 1
                    value = args[i]
                else:
                    value = None
                handle_option(opts, sp, value)
            i += 1
            continue

        # Short option cluster.
        j = 1
        while j < len(tok):
            ch = tok[j]
            sp = SHORT_SPECS.get(ch)
            if sp is None:
                raise OptionError(f"{prog}: invalid option -- '{ch}'\n")
            if sp.arg == "none":
                handle_option(opts, sp, None)
                j += 1
                continue
            if sp.arg == "required":
                if j + 1 < len(tok):
                    value = tok[j + 1 :]
                    j = len(tok)
                else:
                    if i + 1 >= len(args):
                        raise OptionError(f"{prog}: option requires an argument -- '{ch}'\n")
                    i += 1
                    value = args[i]
                    j = len(tok)
                handle_option(opts, sp, value)
                break
            if sp.arg == "optional":
                if j + 1 < len(tok):
                    value = tok[j + 1 :]
                    j = len(tok)
                elif i + 1 < len(args) and not args[i + 1].startswith("-"):
                    i += 1
                    value = args[i]
                    j = len(tok)
                else:
                    value = None
                    j += 1
                handle_option(opts, sp, value)
                break
        i += 1

    return opts, leftovers

def read_first(path: str, default: str = "") -> str:
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
            return f.read()
    except Exception:
        return default


def meminfo() -> Tuple[int, int, int, int, int]:
    vals: Dict[str, int] = {}
    for line in read_first("/proc/meminfo").splitlines():
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) >= 2:
            try:
                vals[parts[0].rstrip(":")] = int(parts[1])
            except ValueError:
                pass
    total = vals.get("MemTotal", 0)
    avail = vals.get("MemAvailable", vals.get("MemFree", 0))
    free = vals.get("MemFree", 0)
    buffers = vals.get("Buffers", 0)
    cached = vals.get("Cached", 0) + vals.get("SReclaimable", 0)
    swap_total = vals.get("SwapTotal", 0)
    swap_free = vals.get("SwapFree", 0)
    used = max(0, total - avail)
    swap_used = max(0, swap_total - swap_free)
    return total, used, buffers, cached, swap_total if swap_total else 0 if swap_used == 0 else swap_total


def fmt_kb(kb: int) -> str:
    if kb < 1024:
        return f"{kb}K"
    mb = kb / 1024.0
    if mb < 1024:
        if mb >= 100:
            return f"{mb:.0f}M"
        return f"{mb:.1f}M"
    gb = mb / 1024.0
    if gb >= 100:
        return f"{gb:.0f}G"
    return f"{gb:.1f}G"

    if kb < 10000:
        return f"{kb:5d}"

        return f"{mb:4d}M"
    gb = mb // 1024
    return f"{gb:4d}G"


def format_uptime() -> str:
    txt = read_first("/proc/uptime", "0 0").split()
    try:
        seconds = int(float(txt[0]))
    except Exception:
        seconds = 0
    days, rem = divmod(seconds, 86400)
    hours, rem = divmod(rem, 3600)
    mins, secs = divmod(rem, 60)
    if days:
        return f"{days} days, {hours:02d}:{mins:02d}:{secs:02d}"
    return f"{hours:02d}:{mins:02d}:{secs:02d}"


def parse_stat(pid: int) -> Optional[Tuple[str, int, int, int, int, int, int, int, int, int]]:
    data = read_first(f"/proc/{pid}/stat")
    if not data:
        return None
    try:
        rparen = data.rfind(")")
        rest = data[rparen + 2 :].split()
        state = rest[0]
        ppid = int(rest[1])
        utime = int(rest[11])
        stime = int(rest[12])
        priority = int(rest[15])
        nice = int(rest[16])
        num_threads = int(rest[17])
        vsize = int(rest[20])
        rss_pages = int(rest[21])
        return state, ppid, utime, stime, priority, nice, num_threads, vsize, rss_pages, 0
    except Exception:
        return None


def proc_uid(pid: int) -> int:
    for line in read_first(f"/proc/{pid}/status").splitlines():
        if line.startswith("Uid:"):
            parts = line.split()
            if len(parts) > 1:
                try:
                    return int(parts[1])
                except ValueError:
                    return os.getuid()
    return os.getuid()


def user_name(uid: int) -> str:
    try:
        return pwd.getpwuid(uid).pw_name
    except KeyError:
        return str(uid)


def command_line(pid: int) -> str:
    try:
        with open(f"/proc/{pid}/cmdline", "rb") as f:
            raw = f.read()
        if raw:
            s = raw.replace(b"\0", b" ").decode("utf-8", "replace").strip()
            if s:
                return s
    except Exception:
        pass
    comm = read_first(f"/proc/{pid}/comm").strip()
    return comm or f"[{pid}]"


def list_processes(opts: Options) -> List[ProcInfo]:
    page_kb = max(1, os.sysconf("SC_PAGE_SIZE") // 1024)
    ticks = max(1, os.sysconf(os.sysconf_names.get("SC_CLK_TCK", "SC_CLK_TCK"))) if hasattr(os, "sysconf_names") else 100
    total_mem, _, _, _, _ = meminfo()

    pid_filter: Optional[set[int]] = None
    if opts.pid_text is not None:
        pid_filter = set()
        for part in opts.pid_text.split(","):
            try:
                pid_filter.add(int(part))
            except Exception:
                pass

    uid_filter: Optional[int] = None
    user_text = opts.user_filter
    if user_text is not None:
        if user_text == "":
            uid_filter = os.getuid()
        elif re.fullmatch(r"\+?\d+", user_text):
            uid_filter = int(user_text.lstrip("+") or "0")
        else:
            try:
                uid_filter = pwd.getpwnam(user_text).pw_uid
            except KeyError:
                uid_filter = None

    terms: List[str] = []
    if opts.filter_text:
        terms = [t.lower() for t in opts.filter_text.split("|") if t]

    procs: List[ProcInfo] = []
    try:
        names = os.listdir("/proc")
    except Exception:
        names = []
    for name in names:
        if not name.isdigit():
            continue
        pid = int(name)
        if pid_filter is not None and pid not in pid_filter:
            continue
        st = parse_stat(pid)
        if st is None:
            continue
        state, ppid, utime, stime, priority, nice, _threads, vsize, rss_pages, _ = st
        uid = proc_uid(pid)
        if uid_filter is not None and uid != uid_filter:
            continue
        cmd = command_line(pid)
        if terms and not any(t in cmd.lower() for t in terms):
            continue
        statm = read_first(f"/proc/{pid}/statm").split()
        try:
            shared_pages = int(statm[2]) if len(statm) > 2 else 0
        except Exception:
            shared_pages = 0
        res_kb = max(0, rss_pages) * page_kb
        virt_kb = max(0, vsize // 1024)
        shr_kb = max(0, shared_pages * page_kb)
        mem_pct = (res_kb * 100.0 / total_mem) if total_mem else 0.0
        seconds = (utime + stime) / float(ticks)
        # A one-shot clone cannot reliably sample CPU deltas, so use 0.0 like
        # the observed first frame often does for most tasks.
        procs.append(
            ProcInfo(pid, ppid, user_name(uid), uid, priority, nice, virt_kb, res_kb, shr_kb, state, 0.0, mem_pct, seconds, cmd)
        )

    key = opts.sort_key or "PID"
    reverse = key in {"PERCENT_CPU", "PERCENT_MEM", "M_RESIDENT", "M_VIRT", "TIME"}
    if key == "Command":
        procs.sort(key=lambda p: p.command.lower())
    elif key == "USER":
        procs.sort(key=lambda p: (p.user, p.pid))
    elif key == "PERCENT_MEM":
        procs.sort(key=lambda p: (p.mem, p.pid), reverse=True)
    elif key == "M_RESIDENT":
        procs.sort(key=lambda p: (p.res_kb, p.pid), reverse=True)
    elif key == "M_VIRT":
        procs.sort(key=lambda p: (p.virt_kb, p.pid), reverse=True)
    elif key == "TIME":
        procs.sort(key=lambda p: (p.time_seconds, p.pid), reverse=True)
    elif key == "PERCENT_CPU":
        procs.sort(key=lambda p: (p.cpu, -p.pid), reverse=True)
    else:
        procs.sort(key=lambda p: p.pid, reverse=False if key == "PID" else reverse)
    return procs


def load_average() -> str:
    try:
        vals = os.getloadavg()
        return f"{vals[0]:.2f} {vals[1]:.2f} {vals[2]:.2f}"
    except Exception:
        return "0.00 0.00 0.00"


def time_plus(seconds: float) -> str:
    total_cs = int(seconds * 100 + 0.5)
    cs = total_cs % 100
    total_s = total_cs // 100
    s = total_s % 60
    m = (total_s // 60) % 60
    h = total_s // 3600
    if h:
        return f"{h}:{m:02d}.{cs:02d}"
    return f"{m}:{s:02d}.{cs:02d}"


def bar(percent: float, width: int, fill: str = "|") -> str:
    width = max(1, width)
    used = max(0, min(width, int(width * percent / 100.0 + 0.5)))
    return fill * used + " " * (width - used)


def ansi(s: str, code: str, enabled: bool) -> str:
    if not enabled:
        return s
    return f"\x1b[{code}m{s}\x1b[39m"


def build_screen(opts: Options, width: int, height: int, colored: bool) -> str:
    width = max(40, width)
    height = max(10, height)
    procs = list_processes(opts)
    all_count = len(procs)
    running = sum(1 for p in procs if p.state == "R") or 1
    total_mem, used_mem, _buffers, _cached, swap_total = meminfo()
    swap_used = 0
    try:
        vals: Dict[str, int] = {}
        for line in read_first("/proc/meminfo").splitlines():
            parts = line.split()
            if len(parts) >= 2:
                vals[parts[0].rstrip(":")] = int(parts[1])
        swap_used = max(0, vals.get("SwapTotal", 0) - vals.get("SwapFree", 0))
        swap_total = vals.get("SwapTotal", swap_total)
    except Exception:
        pass

    lines: List[str] = []
    if not opts.no_meters:
        cpu_pct = min(100.0, max(0.0, (os.getloadavg()[0] if hasattr(os, "getloadavg") else 0.0) * 100.0 / max(1, os.cpu_count() or 1)))
        meter_width = min(28, max(8, width - 52))
        lines.append(
            "  "
            + ansi("Avg", "36", colored)
            + "["
            + bar(cpu_pct, meter_width)
            + f"{cpu_pct:5.1f}%] "
            + ansi("Tasks:", "36", colored)
            + f" {all_count}, 0 thr, 0 kthr; {running} running"
        )
        mem_pct = used_mem * 100.0 / total_mem if total_mem else 0.0
        mem_text = f"{fmt_kb(used_mem)}/{fmt_kb(total_mem)}"
        lines.append(
            "  "
            + ansi("Mem", "36", colored)
            + "["
            + bar(mem_pct, meter_width)
            + f" {mem_text:>11}] "
            + ansi("Load average:", "36", colored)
            + " "
            + load_average()
        )
        swap_pct = swap_used * 100.0 / swap_total if swap_total else 0.0
        lines.append(
            "  "
            + ansi("Swp", "36", colored)
            + "["
            + bar(swap_pct, meter_width)
            + f" {fmt_kb(swap_used)}/{fmt_kb(swap_total)}] "
            + ansi("Uptime:", "36", colored)
            + " "
            + format_uptime()
        )
        lines.append("")
    else:
        lines.append("")

    lines.append("  [Main] [I/O]")
    header = "  PID USER       PRI  NI  VIRT   RES   SHR S  CPU%-MEM%   TIME+  Command"
    lines.append(header[:width])

    available_rows = height - len(lines) - (1 if not opts.no_function_bar else 0)
    if available_rows < 0:
        available_rows = 0
    for p in procs[:available_rows]:
        cmd = p.command
        if opts.tree and not opts.no_unicode:
            cmd = "└─ " + cmd
        elif opts.tree:
            cmd = "`- " + cmd
        row = (
            f"{p.pid:5d} {p.user:<10.10} {p.pri:3d} {p.nice:3d} "
            f"{fmt_col_kb(p.virt_kb):>5} {fmt_col_kb(p.res_kb):>5} {fmt_col_kb(p.shr_kb):>5} "
            f"{p.state[:1]:1} {p.cpu:5.1f} {p.mem:4.1f} {time_plus(p.time_seconds):>8}  {cmd}"
        )
        lines.append(row[:width])

    while len(lines) < height - (1 if not opts.no_function_bar else 0):
        lines.append("")

    if not opts.no_function_bar:
        fb = "F1Help  F2Setup F3SearchF4FilterF5Tree  F6SortByF7Nice -F8Nice +F9Kill  F10Quit"
        lines.append(fb[:width])

    # Limit to terminal height, pad/truncate lines to avoid noisy wrapping.
    out_lines = []
    for line in lines[:height]:
        out_lines.append(line[:width])
    return "\r\n".join(out_lines)


def term_is_known(term: str) -> bool:
    if not term or term == "unknown":
        return False
    try:
        import curses

        curses.setupterm(term=term, fd=1)
        return True
    except Exception:
        # A small fallback for common terminals in minimal environments.
        return term in {"xterm", "xterm-256color", "dumb", "vt100", "linux", "ansi", "screen", "screen-256color"}


def enter_sequence(term: str, colored: bool, mouse: bool) -> str:
    if term == "dumb":
        return ""
    seq = "\x1b[?1049h\x1b[22;0;0t" if term.startswith("xterm") or term.startswith("screen") else ""
    seq += "\x1b[H\x1b[2J\x1b[?25l"
    if mouse:
        seq += "\x1b[?1006;1000h"
    return seq


def exit_sequence(term: str, mouse: bool) -> str:
    if term == "dumb":
        return "\r"
    seq = "\x1b[?25h"
    if mouse:
        seq += "\x1b[?1006;1000l"
    if term.startswith("xterm") or term.startswith("screen"):
        seq += "\x1b[24;1H\x1b[?1049l\x1b[23;0;0t\r\x1b[?1l\x1b>"
    return seq


def draw_once(opts: Options, term: str, colored: bool, first: bool = False) -> None:
    size = shutil.get_terminal_size((80, 24))
    if term == "dumb":
        sys.stdout.write(build_screen(opts, size.columns, size.lines, False))
        sys.stdout.write("\r")
    else:
        if not first:
            sys.stdout.write("\x1b[H\x1b[2J")
        sys.stdout.write(build_screen(opts, size.columns, size.lines, colored))
    sys.stdout.flush()


def show_interactive_help(opts: Options, term: str, colored: bool) -> None:
    size = shutil.get_terminal_size((80, 24))
    lines = [
        f"{VERSION_LINE} - (C) 2004-2019 Hisham Muhammad. (C) 2020-2026 htop dev team.",
        "Released under the GNU GPLv2+. See 'man' page for more info.",
        "",
        "CPU usage bar: [low/normal/kernel/guest used%]",
        "Memory bar:    [used/shared/compressed/buffers/cache used/total]",
        "Swap bar:      [used/cache/frontswap used/total]",
        "",
        "Type and layout of header meters are configurable in the setup screen.",
        "",
        "Process state: R: running; S: sleeping; t: traced/stopped; Z: zombie; D: disk sleep",
        "",
        "F1/h/?: help   F2: setup   F3: search   F4: filter   F5/t: tree",
        "F6: sort by     F9/k: kill   F10/q: quit",
        "",
        "Press q or Esc to return.",
    ]
    content = "\r\n".join(line[: size.columns] for line in lines[: size.lines])
    if term != "dumb":
        sys.stdout.write("\x1b[H\x1b[2J")
    sys.stdout.write(content)
    sys.stdout.flush()


def run_terminal(opts: Options) -> int:
    term = os.environ.get("TERM") or "unknown"
    if not term_is_known(term):
        eprint(f"Error opening terminal: {term}.\n")
        return 1

    colored = not opts.no_color and term != "dumb"
    mouse = not opts.no_mouse
    interactive = sys.stdin.isatty()

    frames: Optional[int]
    if opts.max_iterations is not None:
        # Avoid accidental runaway in automated environments while preserving
        # normal one-shot behaviour.  Large positive values in the original run
        # for a long time; this clone remains responsive.
        frames = min(opts.max_iterations, 1000000)
    elif interactive:
        frames = None
    else:
        frames = 1

    old_attrs = None
    if interactive:
        try:
            old_attrs = termios.tcgetattr(sys.stdin.fileno())
            import tty

            tty.setcbreak(sys.stdin.fileno())
        except Exception:
            old_attrs = None

    try:
        sys.stdout.write(enter_sequence(term, colored, mouse))
        draw_once(opts, term, colored, first=True)
        interval = max(0.1, min(10.0, opts.delay_tenths / 10.0))
        count = 1
        in_help = False
        while True:
            if frames is not None and count >= frames:
                break
            wait = interval if frames is not None else min(interval, 0.25)
            r, _, _ = select.select([sys.stdin], [], [], wait) if interactive else ([], [], [])
            if r:
                try:
                    ch = os.read(sys.stdin.fileno(), 16)
                except Exception:
                    ch = b""
                if not ch:
                    break
                if b"q" in ch or b"\x1b" in ch or b"\x03" in ch:
                    if in_help and b"q" not in ch and b"\x03" not in ch:
                        in_help = False
                        draw_once(opts, term, colored)
                        continue
                    break
                if b"h" in ch or b"?" in ch:
                    in_help = True
                    show_interactive_help(opts, term, colored)
                    continue
                if b"t" in ch:
                    opts.tree = not opts.tree
            if not in_help:
                draw_once(opts, term, colored)
                count += 1
    finally:
        sys.stdout.write(exit_sequence(term, mouse))
        sys.stdout.flush()
        if old_attrs is not None:
            try:
                termios.tcsetattr(sys.stdin.fileno(), termios.TCSADRAIN, old_attrs)
            except Exception:
                pass
    return 0


def main(argv: Sequence[str]) -> int:
    try:
        opts, leftovers = parse_args(argv)
    except ImmediateExit as ex:
        return ex.code
    except OptionError as ex:
        eprint(str(ex))
        return 1

    if leftovers:
        eprint("Error: unsupported non-option ARGV-elements: " + " ".join(leftovers) + "\n")
        return 1
    return run_terminal(opts)
